module_microarchitecture.name: domino_request_gateway
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Synchronous request-transaction capture and forwarding block in a single clock domain.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Qualify request acceptance with enable, geometry/flow validity, and req_ready, then emit a tagged request bundle with monotonic sequence_id and captured timestamp.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Use simple registered storage for last_sequence_id, request timestamp, and the most recently accepted request metadata; no complex FSM is implied here.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Register req_valid and all request metadata outputs; drive only the clean request transaction associated with an accepted request.
ownership_notes: Owns the request-side sequence counter and timestamp capture behavior.
Does not interpret geometry physically and does not drive its input ports.
Is the source of req_* request metadata forwarded to the external model runtime.

module_microarchitecture.name: domino_response_validator
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Registered response qualification block with simple comparison and envelope checks.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Compare incoming response framing, sequence_id, age against timeout_threshold_cycles, and stream_velocity_mps against the 20 to 55 m/s envelope; accept only fully qualified responses.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Hold the most recent validated response metadata in registers until superseded by a newer validated response; no complex FSM is implied.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Register validated response metadata and status flags; assert response_validated only when framing, freshness, matching sequence, and completeness conditions are all satisfied.
ownership_notes: Owns response qualification results and accepted-response readback.
Does not drive request-side or control-side input fields.
Produces the sole validated response metadata consumed by control synthesis.

module_microarchitecture.name: domino_control_safety_fsm
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Registered safety controller with a minimal command-generation datapath and a single pure combinational clamp stage between registered stages.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use validated response metadata to compute a nominal actuator command candidate, clamp it to [cmd_min, cmd_max], and select safe_state whenever fallback, timeout, out_of_range, stale reject, or fault conditions require it.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Implement the specified states IDLE, REQUEST_SENT, WAIT_RESPONSE, VALIDATE_RESPONSE, COMPUTE_CONTROL, APPLY_CLAMP, Fallback, and FAULT_LATCH using straightforward synchronous state registers and next-state selection; avoid unnecessary sub-state complexity.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Register actuator_command, actuator_command_valid, fallback_active, fault_latched, and fsm_state; allow only the clamp function to be combinational between registered stages; prevent any unvalidated data from reaching actuator_command.
ownership_notes: Owns the safety FSM state register and actuator output decision path.
Does not drive configuration or accepted-response input fields.
Ensures no stale or invalid model data can reach the actuator output.

module_microarchitecture.name: domino_automotive_aero_gateway
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Top-level synchronous integration wrapper and signal ownership boundary for the described child blocks.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Route request metadata into the request gateway, model responses into the validator, and validated outputs into the control FSM using the specified internal top-owned signals only.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain deterministic single-clock-domain integration; no additional hidden state machines are introduced beyond those already specified in child modules.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Expose the specified request/response/model-status/actuator outputs as registered top-level-visible signals, mirroring the child module contracts exactly.
ownership_notes: Owns the internal wiring described by top_level_connections and inter_module_signals.
Acts as the integration boundary for external hardware, model runtime, and diagnostics software.
Does not redefine hierarchy, ports, or filenames.

fsm_intent.description: The safety FSM is explicitly specified and should be implemented as a straightforward registered controller with the listed states and direct transitions. The intent is to move from request acceptance through validation and control computation, and to force deterministic fallback or fault latch behavior on invalid, stale, timed-out, out-of-range, or otherwise unsafe conditions.

output_mapping: req_sequence_id driven from the next monotonic sequence value
req_timestamp driven from captured request timestamp
req_* metadata outputs forwarded unchanged from the accepted request context
last_sequence_id reflects the most recently accepted sequence identifier

internal_storage: Age calculation register or equivalent registered age reference
Status registers for timeout, stale reject, out_of_range, and model_online
output_mapping: accepted_response_* outputs hold the most recently validated response metadata
response_validated asserted only for fully qualified responses
stale_reject asserted on mismatch, age exceedance, or freshness failure
timeout asserted when age exceeds timeout_threshold_cycles
out_of_range asserted when stream_velocity_mps is outside the operating envelope
model_online reflects qualified external model runtime status
actuator_command_next is the pre-clamp control candidate or safe_state selection result
actuator_command is the registered final command after clamp/selection
actuator_command_valid indicates valid nominal or fallback output only
fallback_active indicates deterministic safe fallback selection
fault_latched indicates a latched fault condition
fsm_state exposes the current registered safety state

sequencing_notes: Request acceptance is synchronous and deterministic; accepted requests receive monotonically increasing sequence_id values.
Request timestamp capture occurs at the acceptance event and is retained for response correlation.
Response validation occurs only after request context exists and requires framing validity, matching sequence_id, freshness within timeout_threshold_cycles, and envelope compliance.
Validated response metadata is the only response data allowed to influence control synthesis.
The control FSM advances from request and validation states into computation, clamp, fallback, or fault-latch handling according to the specified conditions.
clear_fault only releases a latched fault when permitted by integration policy; reset always restores deterministic safe initialization behavior.
timing_notes: All logic is intended for a single synchronous clock domain with synchronous reset behavior.
All outputs are registered except the explicitly permitted pure combinational clamp stage between registered stages.
No hidden multi-cycle FSM complexity is implied beyond the explicitly listed safety states.
The implementation should remain deterministic and synthesizable in a standard-cell ASIC flow.
If latency_budget_cycles is exceeded, safety handling should be triggered within one control cycle or less subject to the configured budget.
No floating-point arithmetic is required unless a fixed-point command mapping is intentionally implemented; if so, it should be parameterizable and saturating.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
